1. Scope and parties

These Terms govern your use of the deepfluid platform ("Service") operated by [deepfluid GmbH, address TBD] ("we", "us"). By activating your account you accept these Terms in full.

2. Service description

The Service provides optical fluid contamination analytics, including real-time air-in-oil monitoring via the SBS Inline Sensor, lab testing via the SBS AIO device, data aggregation, and reporting. Feature availability depends on your subscription and paired hardware.

3. Account and access

Accounts are created by invitation from your Tenant Admin. You are responsible for:

  • maintaining the confidentiality of your credentials;
  • all activity carried out under your account;
  • notifying us immediately of any unauthorized access.

4. User obligations

You agree not to:

  • reverse engineer, copy, or redistribute the Service;
  • use the Service for unlawful purposes or in violation of applicable regulations;
  • interfere with or disrupt platform security, performance, or data integrity;
  • manipulate calibration data, sensor firmware, or session records.

5. Intellectual property and sensor data

The platform software, algorithms, and branding remain our property. You retain ownership of your measurement data. You grant us a limited, non-exclusive license to process this data to operate the Service, train detection models on anonymized subsets, and provide you with analytical results.

6. Fees and billing

Subscription fees are defined in your Order Form. Fees are invoiced in advance and non-refundable. We may adjust pricing with 60 days notice for subsequent billing periods.

7. Limitation of liability

The Service provides measurement and analytical data as an aid to decision-making. We are not liable for operational decisions made based on the data. Our total liability is limited to the fees paid in the twelve months preceding the claim.

8. Term and termination

Either party may terminate with 30 days written notice. Upon termination, you may export your data for 90 days, after which data is deleted in line with our Privacy Policy.

9. Governing law

These Terms are governed by German law. Jurisdiction is [city TBD], Germany. Mandatory consumer protection laws in your country remain unaffected.

Version 1.0 · Effective: [to be published] · Last updated: 12 March 2026

1. Who we are

[deepfluid GmbH, address TBD] — operator of the deepfluid platform.

Contact: privacy@deepfluid.io

2. What data we collect

  • Account data — name, email, role (required for authentication and audit)
  • Profile preferences — focus areas, notification preferences (optional, for personalisation)
  • Usage data — actions in the platform, logged for security and audit
  • Technical data — IP address, browser type, timestamps (for security monitoring)
  • Measurement data — sensor readings, snapshots, calibration records (your operational data)

3. Legal basis (GDPR Art. 6)

  • Contract performance — account and measurement data required to provide the Service
  • Legitimate interests — security monitoring, audit logging, fraud prevention
  • Consent — optional profile preferences and marketing communications

4. Who we share data with

We do not sell your data. It is shared only with:

  • Your Tenant Admin (activity logs, role assignments)
  • Infrastructure providers (AWS / Hetzner) under a Data Processing Agreement
  • Authorities if required by law

5. Your rights (GDPR Art. 15–22)

You may request at any time:

  • access to your personal data;
  • rectification of inaccurate data;
  • erasure ("right to be forgotten");
  • restriction of processing;
  • data portability in machine-readable format;
  • objection to processing based on legitimate interests.

6. Data retention

Account data is retained for the duration of the contract plus 3 years for audit purposes. Measurement data is retained according to your subscription. After account closure you have 90 days to export data before automated deletion.

7. Cookies and tracking

We use strictly necessary cookies for authentication and session management. We do not use third-party advertising or analytics trackers. Optional product analytics (anonymized) can be disabled in your profile settings.

8. Contact & complaints

For any request, contact privacy@deepfluid.io. You also have the right to lodge a complaint with your local Data Protection Authority.

Version 1.0 · Effective: [to be published] · Last updated: 12 March 2026
Need clarification? Contact legal@deepfluid.io

1. Acceptance of Terms

By creating an account and using the deepfluid platform, you agree to be bound by these Terms & Conditions. If you do not agree, you must not access or use the service.

2. Service Description

deepfluid provides optical real-time contamination analytics for industrial fluids, including air content detection, bubble analysis, water contamination, and particle classification via SBS Inline and SBS AIO devices.

3. User Accounts & Access

Access is by invitation only. Users must:

  • Maintain accurate account information
  • Keep credentials confidential
  • Not share access with unauthorised parties
  • Notify deepfluid promptly of any suspected breach

4. Data & Measurement Ownership

All measurement data generated within your workspace remains the property of your organisation. deepfluid processes this data solely to provide the service. Aggregated, anonymised statistics may be used for algorithm improvement and benchmarking.

5. Acceptable Use

You agree not to:

  • Reverse engineer or attempt to extract proprietary algorithms
  • Use the service for illegal or harmful activities
  • Interfere with platform security or integrity
  • Resell or redistribute access without written consent

6. Service Availability

deepfluid targets 99.5 % monthly uptime. Scheduled maintenance is announced with at least 48 hours notice. No uptime guarantees are provided during beta phases.

7. Limitation of Liability

Measurements are provided as analytical support. Operational decisions based on deepfluid data remain the responsibility of the user. Liability is limited to fees paid in the preceding 12 months.

8. Termination

Either party may terminate with 30 days written notice. Upon termination, measurement data can be exported within 60 days, after which it will be deleted per Privacy Policy §6.

9. Governing Law

These terms are governed by German law. Disputes shall be resolved exclusively in the courts of Mannheim, Germany.

Last updated: 01 March 2026 · Version 3.0 · Contact: legal@deepfluid.io

1. Who we are

deepfluid GmbH (i.Gr.) — operator of the deepfluid platform.

Contact: privacy@deepfluid.io

2. What data we collect

  • Account data — name, email, job position (required for authentication)
  • Profile preferences — role, goals, measurement focus (optional, for dashboard personalisation)
  • Usage data — actions in the platform, logged for security and audit purposes
  • Technical data — IP address, browser type, timestamps (for security monitoring)
  • Measurement data — sensor readings, images, device metadata (processed on behalf of your organisation)

3. Legal basis (GDPR)

  • Contract performance — account data to provide the service (Art. 6 (1) (b) GDPR)
  • Legitimate interests — security monitoring, audit logging (Art. 6 (1) (f) GDPR)
  • Consent — optional profile preferences (Art. 6 (1) (a) GDPR)

4. Who we share data with

We do not sell your data. It is shared only with your Tenant Admin (activity logs, role), infrastructure providers under DPA, and authorities if required by law.

5. Your rights

Under GDPR you may request:

  • Access to, correction of, or deletion of your personal data
  • Restriction of or objection to processing
  • Data portability in a machine-readable format
  • Withdrawal of consent at any time (without affecting past lawful processing)

6. Data retention

  • Account data — for the duration of the contract + 3 years (legal retention)
  • Measurement data — controlled by your Tenant Admin, default retention 7 years
  • Audit logs — 12 months
  • Technical logs — 30 days

7. International transfers

Your data is hosted in the EU (Frankfurt, Germany). Any transfer outside the EEA is secured through Standard Contractual Clauses.

8. Security

TLS 1.3 encryption in transit, AES-256 at rest, role-based access control, continuous security monitoring, regular third-party penetration tests.

Executive Summary · KPIs

During Q1 2026, the Press Line Quality project monitored hydraulic oil contamination across three press lines and one lab reference bench. Continuous inline air-in-oil readings remained within the operational threshold (3% warn / 6% alert) with the exception of one alert event on 24 March on Press Line A.

Lab reference benchmarks (ISO 9120 air release T₅₀ & T₉₀) were performed monthly on representative samples and consistently fell within ISO range, confirming oil chemistry stability.

deepfluid · Quality Report
REP-2026-0042 · Generated 22 Mar 2026 · Hermann Bantleon GmbH

1Executive Summary

During Q1 2026, the Press Line Quality project monitored hydraulic oil contamination across three press lines and one lab reference bench at Hamburg Hall 1. Continuous inline air-in-oil readings remained within the operational threshold (3% warn / 6% alert) with the exception of one alert event on 24 March on Press Line A.

Lab reference benchmarks (ISO 9120 air release T₅₀ & T₉₀) were performed monthly on representative samples and consistently fell within ISO range, confirming oil chemistry stability throughout the quarter.

Key Performance Indicators
2.7%

1
Alert events
2:08
Avg T₅₀ (lab) · ISO range
94%
Coverage · daily reporting
⚠ One alert event documented
Press Line A on 24 March — air content peaked at 7.3%, exceeded alert threshold for 1m 18s. Investigation report: REP-2026-0041

2Project Overview

The Press Line Quality 2026 project includes 4 deployed devices monitoring hydraulic oils on three production presses (Line A, B, C) and one quality control bench (QC Bench A). All devices use Shell Tellus S2 M 46 (HLP · ISO VG 46) as standard hydraulic fluid.
